title: Learn with Keating
description: Turn a topic into a lesson, explain your thinking, and decide what to practice next.

sections.heading: Start with something you want to be able to do
paragraphs: Open chat and describe your goal, what you already know, and where you get stuck. A concrete goal gives Keating more to work with than a subject name alone. You can ask for an explanation, a lesson plan, a concept map, a quiz, or flashcards in ordinary language.
For example: I understand fractions, but I get lost when solving equations. Help me solve a simple equation, then give me a new one to try without showing the answer.

sections.heading: Choose a useful first prompt
paragraphs: Copy one of these examples into chat and replace the subject with your own. They are starting points for a conversation; the response depends on your selected model.
bullets: Learn: Teach me supply and demand using a familiar example. Ask me to predict what happens before explaining it.
Plan: Plan four weeks of beginner machine learning study. Ask about my available time and maths background first.
Map: Show me how probability, statistics, and linear algebra connect in data science.
Explain back: Ask me to explain async/await from scratch, then help me find gaps in my explanation.
Create practice: Make flashcards for the Spanish verb forms I keep confusing.

sections.heading: Work through the question before moving on

screenshots.alt: A tutor reply with a two-choice quick check about recursive calls.
screenshots.caption: A scripted tutor asks for a prediction in Chat before explaining how a call returns.

paragraphs: When Keating presents an interactive question, answer in that activity. A single question uses Send answer; a grouped check ends with Finish check. Explain the step you are unsure about instead of guessing what the tutor wants to hear.

If the explanation moves too quickly, ask for one smaller step, a different example, or a hint. If it feels familiar, ask for a new case that changes an assumption. Finish by explaining the idea without looking back, then compare your explanation with the lesson.

videos.title: A lesson in chat
videos.caption: Watch Alex answer a quick check, rate flashcard recall, run a countdown and retry a reply from the scripted demo tutor.

sections.heading: Tell Keating what helps you learn

screenshots.alt: What Keating is told appears beside the Teaching preferences in Your profile.
screenshots.caption: Review the context that accompanies tutor requests before you save your profile.

screenshots.alt: The signed-out public profile editor shows Alex’s draft and the sign-in notice.
screenshots.caption: You can preview changes before signing in. Sign in before leaving to keep them.

paragraphs: Open Settings, choose Learning, and open Your profile. Add useful context such as your goals, prior knowledge, preferred examples, languages, or accessibility needs, then choose Save profile. The saved setting lives in this browser and applies to the current conversation on your next message and to new sessions.
Within Your profile, open Teaching to choose how Keating helps when you get stuck. Expand What Keating is told before saving to see the context Keating uses.

videos.title: Set your learning preferences
videos.caption: Choose a teaching preference and read the tutor context. See how the separate public-profile preview looks without publishing.

sections.heading: Check what the feedback actually establishes
paragraphs: A tutor explanation or model verdict is feedback to examine. Ask which step supports the conclusion and try the problem yourself. A generated answer key, a model review, and an independently computed mathematical result provide different kinds of evidence.

Some structured arithmetic and linear-equation answers can be checked by a separate exact calculator. Other mathematics can continue through the lesson and receive model feedback with the label Not independently checked. That label means the independent checker did not establish the result; it does not by itself mean your answer is wrong.

After a useful session, return later and try a fresh problem without the explanation in front of you. An encouraging response or a high quiz score alone does not establish that you will retain the idea or apply it elsewhere.

title: Use quizzes and practice
description: Answer interactive questions, interpret grading, and use flashcards for honest recall practice.

sections.heading: Ask for practice that targets a gap
paragraphs: Tell Keating the topic and what you want to test. For example: Quiz me on the Krebs cycle. Ask questions that test deeper understanding, then help me revisit the parts I miss. For a shorter check, ask one question at a time and explain your reasoning.

Questions may ask you to choose an answer, choose several answers, fill blanks, arrange items, or write an explanation. Follow the instructions on the current activity; a text explanation needs different review from a choice with a supplied answer key.

videos.title: Try a quick check in chat
videos.caption: Alex makes a prediction and tries the check again after a hint from the scripted demo tutor.

screenshots.alt: Your response in the chat transcript shows the answer submitted to the recursion check.
screenshots.caption: After you choose Finish check, your answer appears in the conversation.

sections.heading: Answer, flag, and review before submitting
paragraphs: In an interactive chat quiz, use Next to move forward and Previous question to return. Flag for review marks a question you want to revisit. Skip records that you are leaving it unanswered. Review opens the answer list, where you can return to a question before choosing Submit quiz.

Answer or skip every question to submit. If the quiz has a timer, running out of time advances to the next question and keeps the answer already entered. You can return and answer the timed-out question. A Quick marker describes timing; accuracy is scored separately.

sections.heading: Read the score and the grading status together
paragraphs: Questions with a usable objective check can be scored immediately. Open-ended answers wait for the tutor model to grade them. Awaiting your teacher's review and awaiting grading refer to this pending model feedback; they do not mean a human teacher has reviewed your work.

The summary counts answers that have been scored and keeps pending answers separate until a grade arrives. Open Your answers to revisit what you submitted. If feedback is unclear, ask Keating to explain the specific step behind its correct, partial, or incorrect verdict.

screenshots.alt: Quiz with completed grading and feedback.
screenshots.caption: Current component capture with authored fixture data (2026-10-01). A graded quiz displays feedback alongside the learner response.

sections.heading: Understand independently checked maths
paragraphs: For supported structured arithmetic and single-variable linear equations, Keating can compute an exact result separately from the model and compare your numeric answer with it. This checks the represented problem and final answer; it does not independently verify every explanation or proof in the conversation.

If a problem or answer format is outside the checker's supported range, continue answering normally. Unsupported maths may receive a model verdict while keeping Not independently checked beside it. An unsupported check is not an automatic incorrect answer.

For a supported numeric problem, try a plain number or fraction if your answer was not understood. For a proof, a more general equation, or another unsupported problem, include your reasoning and ask for model review. Keep the distinction between that feedback and independent verification visible.

sections.heading: Rate flashcards by what you recalled
paragraphs: Try to recall the answer before choosing Reveal answer or turning the card over. Then choose Again if you missed it, Hard if recall was strained, Good if you recalled it, or Easy if it was immediate. Your rating helps schedule the card's next review.

Use Coming up to find cards that are due. Start due review works through due cards, while Review this deck focuses on one deck. Rate the recall you actually managed, rather than how familiar the answer looks after revealing it.

screenshots.alt: The desktop inline card has a revealed answer and recall rating buttons.
screenshots.caption: Reveal a card in Chat and rate how well you remembered the answer.

screenshots.alt: The answer and recall ratings on a flashcard in narrow Chat.
screenshots.caption: Reveal the card’s answer, then estimate how well you recalled it.

videos.title: Find cards that are due
videos.caption: Open Coming up, reveal a sample card, and rate your recall. The same walkthrough also shows the private benchmark case bank.

sections.heading: Recover a quiz or answer that did not save
paragraphs: If completion could not be delivered, the activity may offer Retry save quiz, Retry save answers, or Retry save deck. Use the retry control after restoring the connection or provider access. Keep the activity open while recovering the saved attempt.

If the activity itself cannot be displayed, use Retry interaction when offered. You can also tell Keating which question failed and ask for a simpler presentation. A broken activity display or a pending grade does not establish that your answer was incorrect.

title: Work with courses and sharing
description: Find course work, save submissions, invite collaborators, and choose between shared study rooms and private continuations.

sections.heading: Open a course workspace
paragraphs: Courses brings lessons, source material, practice, notes, and assignments together. Open an existing course or follow the invitation link supplied by its organiser. Which editing and collaboration controls you see depends on your course role and permissions.

If an access screen appears, read its message. Retry course access checks a failed connection again; Check account is shown when account access is needed. Hosted course workspaces may be unavailable in the running deployment. These controls do not establish that a hosted subscription is available to buy.

links.label: Walkthrough chapters · Post a lesson comment

videos.title: Build and use a course
videos.caption: Create a blank course, then use a sample outline to read a lesson, mark it complete, comment, and inspect the owner-entered work.

screenshots.alt: The Read, Discuss, Review and Build tabs stay at the top when Lesson complete appears at the bottom.
screenshots.caption: After marking a lesson complete, use the tabs at the top to switch to Discuss or Review.

sections.heading: Use a course to organise repeated study

screenshots.alt: The course assembler with title, description and available building blocks.
screenshots.caption: Use Or assemble manually to open the assembler and choose how to start the course.

paragraphs: Select a lesson in the course workspace to read its material and work with the practice or assignments attached to it. Check the task instructions, deliverables, and any opening or due dates before beginning. Keep a question tied to the lesson specific: ask about the passage or step that is blocking you.

When creating a course, give it a concrete learning goal and a manageable scope. The New course builder is a starting point for assembling material you can return to. Review generated lessons and questions for accuracy and fit before inviting other people to rely on them.

sections.heading: Save a draft, then submit deliberately
paragraphs: In an assignment, write your response and attach any required files. Save draft keeps a working revision; Submit records a submission. The attachment control allows up to 10 files of 25 MB each. Wait for files to finish saving before submitting.

Saved on this device confirms local saving. Delivered to course confirms that the course received the work. If delivery is queued or fails, keep your local copy and use Retry delivery after reconnecting. A local save is useful protection, but it is not confirmation that a teacher can see the submission.
Check Share submission with peers only when you want peer sharing for that submission. Review that choice before sending, especially when your response or attachments contain personal material.

screenshots.alt: Assignment showing a submitted learner response.
screenshots.caption: Current component capture with authored fixture data (2026-10-01). The task displays a submitted fixture response.

screenshots.alt: Submission status reading Saved on this device.
screenshots.caption: Current component capture with authored fixture data (2026-10-01). Local saving and course delivery have separate visible states.

screenshots.alt: Submission status reading Delivered to course.
screenshots.caption: Current component capture with authored fixture data (2026-10-01). The delivered status is demonstrated with fixture state; no real course receives a submission.

sections.heading: Invite people with the right role
paragraphs: If your course permissions include inviting members, choose Invite. In Invite to this course, choose a role and use Create link and QR code, then Copy link. The dialog states the invitation's expiry and use limit.

Students work through lessons and control teacher access. Peers can co-work and comment, with deck editing governed by course settings. Teachers can edit lessons, invite members, and request fuller learner visibility. Choose the role that matches the work the person should be able to do.

sections.heading: Study with a group or continue privately
paragraphs: A study room is a shared conversation with classmates, teachers, and Keating. Course teachers can create a room from a lesson's Study rooms section; course members can review its join disclosure and join without another invitation. Standalone study groups use role-based invitation links and QR codes.

To work through a passage on your own, choose Continue privately below the lesson reading or on a public message when you are a learner in a room. Choose an exact excerpt, optionally prepare a question, and open your own Chat. The source stays shared; the private continuation does not complete a lesson or submit course work.

links.label: Use study rooms and private continuations

sections.heading: Share a tutoring session as a snapshot
paragraphs: Open the Chat More menu and choose Share session to share a conversation. The Share session sheet describes what will be included and who can open the link. To change the link mode, open Settings → Data and support → What leaves this device. Public modes upload or embed the visible conversation, supported session artifacts, and finalized review feedback so anyone with the link can read them. Local links work only from that browser's cache.

Review the visible conversation and any finalized feedback before confirming public sharing. The snapshot excludes drafts and hidden tool traffic, and unsupported or oversized artifacts may be omitted. Read the sharing result and any omission notice instead of assuming every attachment or artifact travelled with the link.

sections.heading: Continue from a shared lesson
paragraphs: A shared session opens as a read-only view. Choose Start from this to create your own chat from the shared conversation. This gives you a place to ask follow-up questions without editing the shared snapshot.

If someone cannot open your link, check whether you selected a local link. For a portable link, copy the complete URL and ask the recipient to try it again. A missing session snapshot may require a fresh share link.

title: Study together and continue privately
description: Join a shared study room, understand teacher oversight, and take a chosen passage into your own Chat.

sections.heading: Join or create a room
paragraphs: Open Rooms in the web app, or follow an invitation link from the organiser. Before joining, read who can see the transcript, which teachers oversee the room, and whose AI provider processes messages. Choose a display name and confirm the role shown on the join screen.

To start a standalone group, choose New room and set its title, topic, and goal. The Invite panel creates links and QR codes with a role, expiry, and use limit. A course owner or teacher can also open a room from a lesson's Study rooms section. Course members can join through that section after reviewing the disclosure.

videos.title: A study room with a teacher and learner
videos.caption: Morgan sets a one-use invitation and approves a scripted reply that Alex sees in a separate browser profile.

sections.heading: Understand what the room shares
paragraphs: The room has one shared transcript, including earlier messages and replies from Keating. Members can export what they can see. Hosts and teachers can moderate the room, mute or remove members, pause Keating, and review held replies. Observers can read but cannot post or run Keating.

Private teacher guidance and held replies are visible only to hosts and teachers. Joining a room does not give them access to your personal Chat history or course progress. Participation counts describe contributions in the loaded transcript; they do not measure your understanding.

sections.heading: Run Keating from one browser
paragraphs: A permitted member chooses Run Keating from this tab, reads the disclosure naming their configured Chat model, then confirms Use my model access. That browser sends the room context to its chosen model provider and uses its own provider access or credits. Keep the tab open while facilitating.

Teachers' facilitating browsers also send private teacher guidance. Learners' facilitating browsers receive only shared context. The room settings decide who may facilitate; teacher review restricts facilitation to teachers. Members can keep talking while Keating is off.

sections.heading: Take a chosen passage into private Chat
bullets: As a room learner, choose Continue privately on a visible public message from a person or Keating. In a course, choose Continue privately below the lesson reading.

Review the source. Expand Choose a passage to select text in the original-source field; the excerpt above it shows exactly what will be used. Select a nonempty passage of up to 8,000 characters. Use whole source restores the full message or reading when it fits; longer readings require an excerpt.

Optionally enter Your question, then choose Open private Chat. The source stays in the room or lesson. Room context ends at your chosen message and excludes later messages, hidden content, private guidance, and held replies.

Chat opens with the imported context and your question prepared in the composer. Nothing is sent and no model runs merely by opening it. Press Send message when you are ready; the conversation uses your own chosen Chat model.

sections.heading: Accept or dismiss an offer from Keating
paragraphs: Keating may offer you a private continuation from an existing public message. Only you receive it under Your private study offers. Choose Review private offer to inspect its source, or Dismiss offer. Opening it remains your choice.

When teacher review is enabled, a teacher first uses Approve private-study offer or Reject offer. Pausing Keating during a turn can also hold its offer for review. The teacher reviews an invitation to continue privately; they do not edit a private message body or gain access to your subsequent Chat.

Opened offers show Reopen private Chat, which checks your room membership and source access before returning to the same saved continuation without replacing its history. Dismissed offers disappear. An existing saved continuation remains available through normal Chat history even when the room offer cannot reopen it.

sections.heading: Keep the source and privacy boundaries clear
paragraphs: Imported room context and Imported lesson context identify copied source material separately from your own answers. Expand View full imported context to inspect the saved quotation and attribution. Those imported quotations are excluded from learner-evidence extraction; your later answers follow your normal learning settings.

The continuation is saved in normal Chat history with the usual storage, sync, export, and explicit-sharing controls. Room teachers and classmates cannot read it through the room. A shared browser profile can still contain the same local history, and sharing or exporting the private chat may include the copied source. Opening it never completes a lesson or sends a course submission.

sections.heading: Return to the source or recover an error
paragraphs: Return to source room or Return to source lesson opens a new tab at the exact message or lesson reading. For older room messages, use Load earlier source messages until the requested message is loaded. A lesson's current reading may have changed since your private copy was saved.

If the source changed, was hidden, or is no longer available to you, return to the source and choose it again. Keating does not substitute a nearby passage. Your saved private copy remains in Chat history. If no model is configured or your selected model is unavailable, choose or connect one in Chat settings, then retry Open private Chat.

title: Return to sessions and review
description: Find an earlier lesson, revisit due practice, and record evidence about what helped or hindered your learning.

sections.heading: Find a conversation you want to continue
paragraphs: Use Find a session in the sessions panel, or filter by subject. Select a session to reopen it. Open the row’s More menu and choose Rename to give the session a useful title.

Use New in the sessions panel for a fresh topic. Use Fork session when you want a separate continuation of an existing conversation, or Fork session from here on a response to explore a different direction from that point.

videos.title: Find, pin and fork a session
videos.caption: Use search and subject filters, pin a session, fork a reply, open saved materials, and review the sharing consent sheet.

sections.heading: Pick the next useful review

screenshots.alt: Coming up shows two due cards, Start due review and an open sample assignment.
screenshots.caption: Start due review or return to the assignment shown in Coming up.

paragraphs: Coming up combines due flashcards with topics and open checks that may need attention. Start due review begins the cards currently due. Review this deck selects one deck; Practice in chat returns a topic to the tutor.

Changing Learning priority changes what receives attention without changing a card's review date. Recall ratings determine when cards are due. Use this distinction to focus on an upcoming need while keeping an honest record of what you can remember.

sections.heading: Read the original lesson before judging it

screenshots.alt: The Turns list, transcript, selection toolbar and Margin beside a sample recursion lesson.
screenshots.caption: Open Review session to read the transcript beside notes and rubric ratings.

paragraphs: Choose Review session in chat to inspect the teaching record. Use Turns to move between messages and read the learner's question alongside the tutor response. Tool calls and their results help you distinguish what the tutor said it checked from what actually ran.

Use Rendered for normal reading and Raw when you need the exact source text. A useful review points to a concrete moment: an unexplained step, a misleading example, a helpful question, or an answer the tutor accepted too quickly.

sections.heading: Leave an anchored note

screenshots.alt: The selected passage has Problem, Strength, Suggestion and Rewrite actions.
screenshots.caption: Select a passage in Transcript to open the annotation toolbar.

screenshots.alt: The Margin shows a Problem note anchored to a passage with its rationale filled in.
screenshots.caption: Explain why a passage matters, then choose Add note.

paragraphs: Select text in the transcript or an artifact, then choose Problem, Strength, or Suggestion. Explain Why does this matter? and choose Add note. Add detail such as severity or an alternative only when it helps explain your judgement.

Reselect a marked passage and choose Rewrite to open Revise this text. The draft keeps the original text alongside Replacement text. Open Rubric in the Margin to record the ratings and verdict you can support with evidence. Set the review status to Final when you have finished. Choose Save review, then Export to keep a copy.

links.label: Choose a model for assisted review
Walkthrough chapters · Open a rewrite draft

videos.title: Annotate a saved session
videos.caption: Select a passage, add Problem, Strength and Suggestion notes, revisit a marked passage to open a rewrite draft, then inspect the rubric and export.

sections.heading: Treat model-assisted review as a proposal

screenshots.alt: The Socratic pass menu offers Read the session, Score the rubric and Finish this note.
screenshots.caption: Open Socratic pass to see the proposal actions.

paragraphs: The review tools include Read the session, Score the rubric, and Finish this note. These ask a model to propose notes or ratings. Inspect the cited passage, accept the notes you agree with, dismiss the others, and use Apply only when you agree with a proposed rubric assessment.

A model judging another model's lesson is still model review. It does not independently verify all facts or demonstrate that a learner retained the material. Running a model-assisted pass sends review material to the selected model; check the provider you have chosen before starting it.
Use the review to decide what to try next: a clearer explanation, a smaller step, or a new problem that tests whether the idea carries over.

videos.title: Inspect private benchmark evidence
videos.caption: The case bank shows sample replay cases and the benchmark shows that the evidence is too sparse to rank the demo model.

sections.heading: Protect work stored in your browser
paragraphs: Use the same browser profile and app address when returning to local sessions. Another browser, a private window, or another device may not have those records. Clearing site data can remove local work.

If chat warns that storage persistence is not enabled, choose Try again to request it again. The browser may still decline, and local records may be removed under storage pressure. Keep separate copies of work you cannot afford to lose; a local share link is not a backup outside the browser.

title: Use voice and attachments
description: Bring a document, image, or recording into a lesson and recover when speech or file handling fails.

sections.heading: Attach material with a question
paragraphs: In the Chat composer, choose the paperclip button labelled Attach files. Add your file, then say what you want to do with it: explain a passage, examine a diagram, compare two approaches, or make practice from a section. Check the attachment chips before sending and use Remove attachment if you selected the wrong file.

Chat accepts images, audio, readable text files, and PDFs. The selected model must support the input you send. For an image, choose a model that accepts images; a model that only accepts text cannot inspect the picture just because it is attached.

sections.heading: Use PDFs with readable text
paragraphs: Keating extracts text from PDFs for the conversation. A scanned PDF with no readable text needs optical character recognition before attaching. PDF text extraction is not a guarantee that every diagram, layout detail, or equation was preserved.

If a file fails or the model says the conversation is too large, try a smaller excerpt or remove the newest attachment. For a diagram, attach an image with an image-capable model and identify the part you want to discuss. Keep the original file available so you can check the response against it.

sections.heading: Record a message and check the transcript
paragraphs: Choose Record an audio message to open the recording controls. Use Hold to speak, allow microphone access when your browser requests it, and release when finished. Keating attaches the recording and attempts transcription when speech credentials are available.

Read the transcript in the composer before sending and correct names, numbers, or technical terms. Switch to keyboard returns to text input. If transcription fails, the recording can remain attached; the notice says Your audio is still attached when that is the case.

sections.heading: Set up speech or a live conversation

screenshots.alt: Live with Keating preflight with a provider picker and a local deployment readiness notice.
screenshots.caption: Open Live sessions to check provider readiness before pressing Start talking.

paragraphs: Open Settings → Learning → Voice and Live to choose speech options. The speech provider can differ from the main chat model and may need its own credentials. Live conversation requires a compatible live provider and browser microphone access; speech output alone does not establish live conversation support.

To check setup first, open the Chat More menu and choose Live sessions. Check Who you talk to and the readiness message before choosing Start talking. The waveform button labelled Start a live conversation in the composer opens the call directly. Available visual inputs depend on the live provider and model, so use the options shown for your current configuration.

sections.heading: Recover without losing your recording
paragraphs: For Transcript unavailable, check the speech provider credentials and use the offered transcription retry. You may instead send the recording to an audio-capable model. If you want to send only a transcript you typed yourself, remove the audio attachment first.

For a microphone error, check the site's microphone permission and your selected input device, then try recording again. If the optional speech layer fails, turn speech off and continue with text; the main chat model may still work.
An attached recording, a completed transcript, and a successful model response are separate steps. Check which one failed before recording again or removing the attachment.

title: Keep control of your learning data
description: Understand local storage, choose what leaves your device, and export or restore your lessons.

sections.heading: Know where your work is saved
paragraphs: Keating keeps browser conversations, learning artifacts, and settings in browser storage. Provider keys you enter in the website are stored locally too. Another browser profile or device has separate storage.

Study rooms also keep a shared transcript on the room server. A private continuation from a room or lesson is saved in your normal Chat history, with its usual sync, export, and sharing settings. Room membership does not grant access to that private history; using a shared browser profile can still expose the same local records.

A Not Organic account manages hosted access and account credit; signing in is not an automatic backup of your browser's lesson library. Native mobile learning storage is also local to the device. Desktop peer-to-peer sync is a separate device-connection feature, not a promise of account-based cloud backup.
Clearing site data or losing a device can remove local work. Export a copy before changing browsers, deleting app data, or uninstalling.

sections.heading: Understand what leaves the device
paragraphs: When you use a remote model, the prompt and relevant conversation material are sent through the configured connection to the service providing the response. Attachments and speech may also be sent to the services used for those features. Review your chosen provider's data practices before submitting private material.

In a study room, Keating runs from one permitted member's browser using that member's chosen model provider. Review the join disclosure before posting. Continuing privately uses your own chosen Chat model; opening the copied source does not run inference or send a question until you choose Send message.

A browser or native offline model generates locally. Other features you choose, such as sharing, online speech, or optional evaluation sharing, can still send data out. Local generation does not turn those features off.
Keep API keys in credential fields. A key pasted into a conversation becomes conversation content and can be included in a model request, share, or export.

sections.heading: Choose analytics and evaluation settings

screenshots.alt: What leaves this device lists privacy choices, their defaults and destinations.
screenshots.caption: Find disclosure and sharing choices under Data and support.

paragraphs: Open Settings → Data and support → What leaves this device. These preferences apply to the browser where you change them. Controls that are unavailable in the current build explain that in their description.
bullets: Anonymous product analytics controls future product events, such as feature use and response timing. Keating excludes prompts, replies, file contents, provider keys, and full share links from these PostHog events.

Privacy-masked session replay controls interaction recordings where the deployment offers them. Text, inputs, and other sensitive page details are masked. Replay also depends on product analytics being enabled.

Share future turns for Arize evaluation is separate and off by default. Where enabled, it may send the current visible prompt and final visible reply for future turns. Read its description: some deployments permit metadata only. Turn it off to stop future submissions.

sections.heading: Export a copy of your lessons

screenshots.alt: The Export your data confirmation sheet lists included and excluded records and the Portable Keating JSON format.
screenshots.caption: Read what goes into the portable JSON copy and where it will be saved.

paragraphs: Open Settings → Data and support → Your data. Choose Export next to Everything on this device. Read the sheet and choose Export to download the copy. Save the downloaded keating-portable-data.json somewhere you can find from your next device.

The portable export includes saved sessions, learner state, learning artifacts, goals, quizzes, flashcards, and review records. Available sandbox history is included. It does not transfer provider sign-ins, API-key settings, or downloaded model files.
Wait for the export confirmation and check that the file downloaded before clearing any data. The JSON contains your learning content as readable text; store it as carefully as the original notes.

links.label: Open Portable data on Learning usage

videos.title: Inspect and export your data
videos.caption: Read what can leave the browser, prepare a sample dataset with scoring off, and inspect the ZIP, review and portable JSON export sheets.

sections.heading: Restore in another browser
paragraphs: Open Keating in the destination browser, open Settings → Data and support → Your data, and choose Import next to Bring data in. Select your saved export and wait for the import summary. Open a session to check its contents before discarding the original copy.
Export any existing work in the destination browser first. An import writes sessions and records with their saved identifiers, so importing an older copy can replace a matching saved record.
Reconnect model providers on the destination device and download any local models again. A successful data import does not sign you in to those services or restore model downloads.

sections.heading: Share and remove data deliberately
paragraphs: A Share session link makes the shared conversation, supported artifacts, and finalized review feedback readable by anyone with that link. Review the content before confirming a share. A share link is useful for showing someone a lesson; use a portable export to move your learning data.

Use browser site-data controls to remove the website's local data after exporting anything you want to keep. Removing a local copy does not remove shared copies or information already sent to a model provider. Sign out of connected accounts and remove saved credentials when retiring a device.

title: Troubleshoot a learning session
description: Recover provider access, interrupted responses, local saves, course delivery, and offline readiness.

sections.heading: Provider sign-in failed
paragraphs: Open Settings → Models and connections → Providers and keys. Check the credentials for the provider used by the selected chat model. Re-enter an invalid or expired key, or complete the provider's sign-in flow where offered, then retry the failed turn. Check that the selected model belongs to the provider you configured.

Model access is not allowed means the provider account may lack access to that model. Choose a model available to the account or correct its permissions. Provider credits unavailable needs attention in that provider account, or another configured model; repeatedly retrying the same request will not restore credits.
If the error is Voice sign-in failed, check the speech provider separately in Learning → Voice and Live. You can turn speech off and continue with text.

sections.heading: The reply stalls or cannot reach the provider
paragraphs: Keating retries brief network interruptions, timeouts, and temporary provider failures before showing an error. If the error remains, check your connection and any VPN or proxy. If you chose a local model server, confirm that it is running and reachable from the Keating environment you are using.

Use Stop generating to stop a response that is still running before changing direction. Retry after the connection recovers, or choose another configured model if the provider remains unavailable. Respect a rate-limit wait message instead of repeatedly sending the same prompt.
For Conversation is too large for this model, start a focused chat, remove large attachments, or choose a model with a larger context window. Preserve any unsent work before reloading the page.

sections.heading: Sessions are missing or local saving fails
paragraphs: Return to the same browser profile and https://chat.keating.help/, then use Search sessions. A new browser profile or private window may have an empty local history. Do not clear site data as the first troubleshooting step: it can remove the records you are trying to recover.

If the storage persistence warning appears, choose Try again. Browser settings determine whether persistence is granted. If saving fails because storage is full, keep copies of important text and files, free device space without deleting Keating's site data, and retry the save.

For a file attachment failure, read the message and use the offered Retry file or Retry files control. Check the file size and type. Scanned PDFs need readable text, and course submission attachments have a limit of 10 files and 25 MB per file.

sections.heading: Check offline readiness before relying on it
paragraphs: A page opening from cache or a conversation being saved locally does not mean the selected tutor can answer offline. Hosted providers need a connection. A local model also needs its runtime and model files available on the device where it runs.

If your installed desktop build shows Offline tutor under Models and connections, inspect its status. Resume download continues a paused download; Ready offline tells you to choose MiniCPM5 2B (Offline) in the model selector. Offline runtime unavailable in this build means that build cannot provide the offline runtime.

Before depending on offline tutoring, finish setup while connected, select the local model, disconnect, and try a short text conversation. This is a readiness check for your installation, not a promise that an offline installer is currently available. In the desktop offline tutor, images need a vision model and recordings need a transcript.

links.label: Set up the desktop offline tutor

sections.heading: Course work is saved but not delivered
paragraphs: Saved on this device means a local copy exists. Wait for Delivered to course before assuming the course has received it. If delivery is queued, restore the connection and use Retry delivery. Keep the browser's local data and original files until you have confirmed delivery.

If the course itself cannot open, follow the access screen's recovery: Retry course access for a failed check or Check account when account access is required. An unavailable hosted workspace cannot be fixed by repeatedly submitting your work. A course invite that no longer works may need a fresh invitation from the organiser.

sections.heading: An activity is broken or an answer is still awaiting review
paragraphs: Use Retry interaction when an activity cannot display and the control is offered. For a completed activity that could not save, use its specific retry control, such as Retry save quiz. Tell Keating which question failed if you need a simpler version.

Awaiting grading means a model verdict has not arrived. After restoring provider access, ask Keating to review the submitted answers. Not independently checked is different: the mathematical checker did not establish the result, but the lesson can continue and a model can still give a labelled verdict. Neither state alone means you answered incorrectly.

When reporting a persistent problem, include the visible error title, selected provider and model, the action that failed, and whether the problem affects text, voice, an attachment, or course delivery. Remove credentials and private content from any details you share.
